Let's face it, Wadjet Eye's track record of porting their point-and-click adventure games to Linux is spotty at best. They started porting the Blackwell series and then just completely stopped.

Luckily, you can get this game working in Wine pretty easily. Here is the config I used.

Note: This was based on a GOG copy of the game. No idea if the same settings are required to get the game working on the Steam release. Whether or not you obtain the copy legally is for your own conscience to decide. This is just to detail how the game, wherever it came from, can be run.

Wineprefix: 32 or 64bit, set to WinXP or 7. (Could work with higher OS versions, but not tested.)

Wine Version: 3.13 Staging (can work with development and stable releases. Tested as low as 3.3)

Workarounds:

  • Set to run as virtual desktop (fullscreen runs fine, but crashes when switching focus away from the game, such as when alt-tabbing). What resolution you choose is up to you, though the game's native resolution is 640x480, so expect it to look pixelated at pretty much any resolution.
  • Offscreen Rendering Mode - Set to BackBuffer to ensure graphics are displayed correctly in game (characters in shadow at beginning etc...)

Additional Points of Note:

The GOG installer may throw a bunch of error messages at the end of the install, but those can be safely ignored, as it has installed the game.

And that is it. I've played for around 20 minutes into the game and not encountered any other issues so far. This was a 1.0 release of the game, so chances are it has bugs of its own that will be fixed in later patches, but saying that, it is a pretty simple game, from a technological perspective (hell it is using DX5), so I shouldn't expect you would encounter game breaking bugs due to Wine not supporting a certain feature. If you encounter some weirdness, after applying this config, then chances are it is a game bug, not a Wine issue.
